title: Resolve Undo-Redo Text Commands
description:
You are given an array of command strings `commands` applied sequentially to an initially empty text document with undo/redo history:
- `"TYPE <word>"`: appends `<word>` (a non-empty lowercase string) to the end of the document, records this action on the undo stack, and **clears the redo stack**.
- `"UNDO"`: if the undo stack is non-empty, pops the most recent `TYPE` action, removes its appended text from the end of the document, and pushes it onto the redo stack (otherwise does nothing).
- `"REDO"`: if the redo stack is non-empty, pops the most recent undone action, re-appends its text to the document, and pushes it back onto the undo stack (otherwise does nothing).

Return the final text document as a single string.
constraints: Each command is 'UNDO', 'REDO', or 'TYPE <word>' where <word> consists of 1 to 20 lowercase English letters.
hints: Maintain two stacks of strings: `undoStack` holding the currently active typed chunks in order, and `redoStack` holding chunks removed by UNDO.
Remember that any new `TYPE` command must clear `redoStack`, and the final document is simply the concatenation of `undoStack` from bottom to top.

examples.explanation: Type "hi", type "there", undo removes "there", redo restores "there", yielding "hithere".
Undo removes "world", then typing "algo" clears the redo stack, so the subsequent REDO does nothing, leaving "helloalgo".
UNDO and REDO on empty stacks are safely ignored, leaving "ok".
